questions.q: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains anerror in phrasal verb.
o: Tina dropped behind of
into a good job
questions.s:
Correct answer:Tina dropped behind of

Explanation:

The phrasal verb "drop behind" means to fall behind in progress, especially in studies or work. However, it is not followed by "of."

Correct usage: "drop behind in (something)"
For example: She dropped behind in her studies.

Let’s break down the error:

  • "Dropped behind of" – ❌ incorrect; "of" should not follow the phrasal verb "drop behind"

  • Correct form would be: "Tina dropped out of college..." if the intended meaning is she left college

  • If the meaning is she fell behind academically, it should be: "dropped behind in college"

But since she "went straight into a good job," the intended meaning is that she left college, so the correct phrasal verb is:
"dropped out of college"

Correct sentence:
"Tina dropped out of college and went straight into a good job."

Therefore, the segment "Tina dropped behind of" contains the error.

questions.q: Ramesh is smarter (a)/enough to get (b)/selected for this (c)/post, without any recommendations. (d)
The dead is remembered through the legacy they leave behind.
o: The dead is remembered
questions.s:
When ‘the’ is used before an adjective, the adjective becomes a plural common noun. It will hence take a plural verb. These adjectives are Rich, poor, needy, aged, blind, dead, meek, wicked, etc. The correct option is (a) "The dead is remembered."

The correct sentence should be: "The dead are remembered through the legacy they leave behind."

questions.q: She is the most experienced of the two candidates.
o: She is the most
questions.s:
If one is chosen out of two, we use a comparative degree preceded by ‘the’ and followed by ‘of’. So, the correct choice is: She is the most.

The correct answer would be: “She is the more experienced of the two candidates.”

questions.q: Select the most appropriate form of comparative degree that can substitute the underlined segment in the given sentence.
o: as good as the most other batsmen
the best batsmen
better than most other batsmen
questions.s:
Answer: better than most other batsmen

Explanation:
The sentence:
"Rohit Sharma is better than more other batsman in the world."

  • The correct comparative form is "better than most other batsmen."

  • "More other" is incorrect; "most other" or "most of the other" is used.

  • "Batsmen" is plural.

Other options:

  • Better batsmen – incomplete phrase

  • As good as the most other batsmen – awkward and incorrect

  • The best batsmen – superlative, not comparative

Correct sentence:
"Rohit Sharma is better than most other batsmen in the world."
